headline: Charleston County has said nothing since Nov 19 on what data was taken or who was behind the cyberattack.
summary: Not checked: access blocked. Charleston County's own pages (s001, s002 and charlestoncounty.gov) returned a block page ('You are blocked from accessing this Web page') and were not re-read. Holy City Sinner (Nov 21) reproduces the county's update in full and matches the Nov 19 release: SLED criminal investigation, extent of data still being determined, operations unaffected. SC Public Radio (s003) returned only navigation text. No county or SLED statement after Nov 19 found, no notice to residents, no attribution or ransom claim (q003, q004 Not established). A separate 2024 school-district ransomware incident in search results was set aside. No rumors found.
author: Research agent

headline: SLED confirmed its role to WCIV; state breach-notice rule added. No label change.
summary: Added WCIV's Nov 18 report (s009): SLED confirmed to the station that its assistance began Tuesday, Nov 17, and is ongoing, our first statement from SLED itself rather than through the county. It covers SLED's assistance, not the criminal-investigation status, which still rests on the county's Nov 19 release (c004). The same report says South Carolina law requires notices to affected residents and a report to the state Department of Consumer Affairs above 1,000 residents; no notice for the county has been reported (c006, q003). County releases unchanged (Nov 17, Nov 19). No root cause, attribution, data type, count or ransom claim reported. Privacy check done: no names of individuals, officials, experts, reporters or spokespeople, no contact details.

headline: County says a sophisticated cyberattack copied data; SLED opened a criminal investigation. Who and what data: not established.
summary: First draft. 8 sources (2 Tier 1, 5 Tier 2, 1 Tier 3), 10 claims (5 Confirmed, 5 Not established), 6 questions. The cyberattack, the copying of data, the SLED criminal investigation and the county's statement that operations are unaffected are Confirmed on the county's own releases, which Tier 2 outlets repeat. What data was taken, who did it, how they got in, and any ransom claim are Not established; we found no claim in news coverage and did not visit any leak site, dark-web page or tracker. A tie to the November outage wave is Not established. Privacy check done: no names of individuals, officials, reporters or spokespeople, no handles or contact details, no phone numbers.
